83:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Mutaffifin In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Aqil informed us. Ibn Majah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr added: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, my father informed me, on the authority of Yazid, who is the son of Abu Sa’id al-Nahwi, a client of the Quraysh, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, they were the worst of people in measuring, so God Almighty revealed: Woe to those who give short measure. So they improved their measuring after that. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja`far ibn al-Nadr ibn Hammad told us, Muhammad ibn `Ubayd told us, on the authority of al-A`mash, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Hilal ibn Talq, who said: While I was walking with Ibn `Umar, I said: Who are the best-looking people and the most full in measure, the people of Mecca or the people of Medina? He said: It is their right. Have you not heard God, the Most High, say: Woe to those who give short measure. Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa`ib told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar, on the authority of `Abdullah al-Maktab, on the authority of a man, on the authority of `Abdullah, who said: A man said to him: O Abu `Abd al-Rahman, the people of Medina give full measure. He said: What prevents them from giving full measure when God, the Most High, said: “Woe to those who give short measure. Who, when they take by measure from people, take in full. But when they give by measure or weight to them, give less. Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day? The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.” What is meant by giving short measure here is short measure and weight, either by increasing it if one takes it from people or by decreasing it if one pays them. For this reason, it was interpreted as God the Almighty has cursed the defrauders whom He promised loss and destruction, which is woe, in His statement: Those who, when they take by measure from people meaning from people, take in full meaning they take their right in full or in excess, but when they give by measure or weight to them, they give less meaning they fall short. It is better to make they measured and they weighed transitive and for they to be in the accusative case. Some of them make it a pronoun emphasizing the hidden word in His statement they measured and they weighed and delete the object because the statement indicates it, and both are similar. God the Almighty has commanded us to be faithful in measuring and weighing, as He says: “And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a balance that is right. That is better and most suitable for final outcome.” And He the Almighty says: “And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not charge any soul except [with that within] its capacity.” And He the Almighty says: And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance. And God destroyed the people of Shu’ayb and ruined them because they cheated people in weights and measures. Then He the Almighty said, threatening them: Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day? Meaning, what do those people fear of resurrection and standing before the One who knows the secrets and consciences on a terrible, frightening, and serious Day, when whoever loses on it will enter a blazing Fire? And God the Almighty says: The Day mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds. Meaning, they will stand barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised in a difficult, difficult, narrow, and straitened situation for the sinner, and they will be overwhelmed by the command of God the Almighty in a way that their powers and senses are incapable of handling. Imam Malik narrated from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds until one of them will be submerged in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Narrated by al-Bukhari from the hadeeth of Malik and Abdullah ibn Awn, both from Nafi’ with this chain of narration. Muslim also narrated it through both chains of narration. Likewise, it was narrated by Ayyub ibn Yahya, Salih ibn Kaysan, Abdullah and Ubaydullah, the sons of Umar, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar with this chain of narration. The wording of Imam Ahmad is: Yazid narrated to us, Ibn Ishaq informed us, from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar, I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “The Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, out of the majesty of the Most Merciful, the Majestic and Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection, until the sweat will bridle men up to the middle of their ears.” Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Ishaq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, on the authority of al-Miqdad, meaning Ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, the sun will be brought near to the servants until it is a distance of one or two miles away - he said - and the sun will melt them and they will be covered in sweat according to the extent of their deeds. Some of them will be drenched in sweat up to their heels, some of them up to their knees, some of them up to their waists, and some of them will be bridled with a bridle.” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of al-Hakam bin Musa on the authority of Yahya bin Hamza, and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Suwayd on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, both of them on the authority of Ibn Jabir with it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan ibn Suwar told us, Al-Layth ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Salih, that Abu Abd al-Rahman told him, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun will draw near on the Day of Resurrection to the length of a mile, and its heat will increase by such-and-such. Vermin will boil from it as pots boil, and they will sweat in it according to the extent of their sins. Some of them will sweat up to their ankles, some up to their shins, some up to their waists, and some will be bridled by sweat.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Abu Ashana Huyayy ibn Ya’min told us that he heard Uqbah ibn Amir say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The sun will come close to the earth and people will sweat. Some people’s sweat will reach their heels, some will reach halfway up their shins, some will reach their knees, some will reach their buttocks, some will reach their waists, some will reach their shoulders, and some will reach the middle of their mouths – and he pointed with his hand and covered his mouth with it. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pointing like this with his hand, and some will be covered in sweat.” He clapped his hand in a gesture. Ahmad alone reported it. In a hadith, they will stand for seventy years without speaking. It was said that they will stand for three hundred years, and it was said that they will stand for forty thousand years, and judgment will be passed between them within the space of ten thousand years, as in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. In Sunan Abi Dawud it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek refuge in God from the narrowness of the place on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Mas’ud narrated that they would stand for forty years, raising their heads to the heavens, and no one would speak to them, and sweat would bridle both the righteous and the wicked. Ibn Umar narrated that they would stand for one hundred years. Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. In Sunan Abi Dawud, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Zayd ibn Al-Habbab, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Azhar ibn Sa’id Al-Hawari, on the authority of Asim ibn Hamid, on the authority of Aisha, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would begin his night prayer by saying: ‘God is great’ ten times, ‘Praise be to God’ ten times, ‘Subhan God’ ten times, ‘Istighfar’ ten times, and ‘O God, forgive me, guide me, provide for me and grant me well-being.’ He would seek refuge from the narrowness of the place on the Day of Resurrection.”

83:7: God Almighty says truly, Indeed, the book of the wicked is in Sijjin, meaning that their destiny and their abode is in Sijjin, which is an active verb from the word sijn, meaning constriction, as one says: a sinner, "a drinker, a drunkard," and the like. That is why its matter is so great, as God Almighty says, "And what will make you know what Sijjin is?" Meaning, it is a great matter, a permanent prison, and a painful torment. Then some have said: It is under the seventh earth, and it was mentioned previously in the hadith of Al-Bara' bin Azib in his long hadith: God Almighty says about the soul of the disbeliever, "Write his book in Sijjin." And the Sijjin is under the seventh earth, and it was said: A green rock under the seventh earth, and it was said: A well in Hell, and Ibn Jarir narrated a strange and rejected hadith about that, and he said: Ishaq bin Wahb Al-Wasiti told us, Masoud bin Musa bin Miskan Al-Wasiti told us, Nasr bin Khuzaymah Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Shuaib bin Safwan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hell, and as for Sijjin, it is open.” What is correct is that Sijjin is taken from the prison, which is narrow, because all of the creatures, whatever is lower than them, is narrow, and whatever is higher than them is spacious. The seven spheres, each one of them is wider and higher than the one below it, and likewise the earths, each one is wider than the one below it, until the absolute lowest and narrowest place ends at the center in the middle of the seventh earth. And since the fate of the wicked is Hell, which is the lowest of the low, as God Almighty said: Then We returned him to the lowest of the low, * Except for those who believed and did righteous deeds. And He said: Here: “No indeed! The record of the wicked is in Sijjin. And what can make you know what is Sijjin?” It combines narrowness and lowliness, as God Almighty said: And when they are thrown therein into a narrow place, chained together, they will cry out there for destruction. The Almighty’s saying: A Book inscribed is not an explanation of His saying: And what can make you know what is the Sijjin? Rather, it is an explanation of what was written for them regarding the destination of the Sijjin, meaning it is inscribed, written, and decided, to which no one may add or subtract. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Then God the Almighty said: "Woe, that Day, to the deniers" meaning when they are on the Day of Resurrection to what God has promised them of prison and humiliating punishment. We have already discussed His statement "Woe" in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it, and that what is meant by that is destruction and devastation, as is said: "Woe to so-and-so", and as came in al-Musnad and al-Sunan from the narration of Bahz ibn Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haidah from his father from his grandfather who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Woe to the one who speaks and lies to make people laugh. Woe to him, woe to him." Then God the Almighty said, explaining the lying, immoral, disbelieving sinners: "Those who deny the Day of Judgment" meaning they do not believe in its occurrence or believe in its existence and they rule it out. God the Almighty said: "And none denies it except every transgressor and sinner" meaning transgressor in his actions by engaging in what is forbidden and exceeding what is permissible and sinful in his words. If he speaks, he lies, if he promises, he breaks his promise, and if he disputes, he is immoral.
